pl210176087.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl210176087.description: An archaeological site with Iron Age funerary megaliths located in the vicinity of the modern Moonamkutty-Mangad Road in the northeastern portion of India's Kollam municipality. The site was damaged by cashewnut tree farming and is now not visible due to habitation on the site.

pl50120.description: Mantai was an ancient coastal town and harbor of northern Sri Lanka.

pl49850.description: The ancient settlement associated with the modern village of Alagankulam on the Vaigai river in Tamil Nadu is thought to have been an ancient seaport though now positioned some 3 kilometers from the coast. The immediate area has produced local and imported ceramics (including Mediterranean amphorae and Roman potsherds), as well as fourth-century Roman coins.

pl49890.description: An ancient port settlement on the southwest coast of India, mentioned by the Periplus, Pliny, and Ptolemy. Casson (whence BAtlas) places it at modern Pirakkād/Purakkad in the state of Kerala.

pl50064.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl50064.description: An ancient settlement of southeastern India associated with trade and pearl fishery in both Sangam and Roman literature (Ptolemy calls it an "emporion"). Although the area -- where chance finds, and excavation have surfaced material ranging in date from the first millennium BCE to at least the second century CE -- now lies some 6km inland from the ocean and 2km north of the current course of the Thamirabharani river, modern scholars uniformly consider it to have been an ancient seaport equipped with a harbor of some kind. Literary sources attest to its importance during the Pandya dynasty.

pl532531493.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl532531493.description: A late medieval port town located in modern Tamil Nadu, India, on the Bay of Bengal. It seems to have flourished from the 13th century until the 17th, with Chinese and Islamic pottery from the first two centuries of that time being most abundant.

pl465741478.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl465741478.description: A modern village located on the Bay of Bengal in Tamil Nadu, just north of the Rameswaram peninsula. Epigraphic and ceramic evidence indicate that the village's antecedent was a thriving locus of maritime trade from the 13th to the 17th centuries CE.

pl444530273.description: A medieval port city on the Bay of Bengal that seems to have replaced ancient Korkai as landscape change modified the course of the Tamiraparani river and the coastline at its delta.

cur-find-keeladi.dateNote: Digs since 2015 at Keeladi, Tamil Nadu, have found brick buildings, drains and pottery with Tamil-Brahmi letters from a Sangam-age town. The Tamil Nadu archaeology department's 2019 report dates the earliest layer to about the 6th century BC; the Archaeological Survey of India has asked for better proof of those dates. Pinned at the Wikidata point for Keezhadi village.
